title: Stabilize VPC fanout token-emission choke during mixed-quant warmstart rollouts
creator: Arielle Gomez
description: Multiple enterprise VPC customers reported abrupt TTFT regressions and tokens/sec collapse during mixed-quant model rollouts. Symptoms: first-token latency increased 2-5x, sustained tokens/sec for affected sessions dropped by 60-80% for 1-3 minutes after cold warmstart, and dashboards show KV cache eviction storms and kernel-selection thrash across fanout shards. Affected deployments: Hosted (multi-tenant fallback path), Dedicated pools with mixed ABI kernels, and Private clusters performing staggered quant swap rollouts. Customers observed spikes coincident with high-concurrency warmstart periods and heterogeneous model variants (int8/int4) being probed in the same request fanout. This ticket coordinates triage, immediate mitigations, and a short-term hotfix to prevent customer-impacting regressions while we implement a robust routing/kernel-selector change.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy mixed-quant model set (one int8 variant + one int4 variant) behind a VPC with fanout enabled and batching at low latency SLOs.
2) Ramp 200 concurrent short-session requests (avg prompt 40 tokens) with staggered arrival patterns to force warmstart overlap.
3) Observe KV cache eviction rate metric >10x baseline and kernel-selection fallback events in infra logs; check TTFT and tokens/sec on per-session traces.
4) Reproduce in Dedicated by toggling weight-probing to 'parallel' so model variants are probed simultaneously against same request.
5) Validate that disabling cross-variant probing or reducing concurrency eliminates the spike.
acceptance_criteria: Immediate mitigation deployed: cross-variant probing is gated during warmstart windows for VPC and Dedicated routes.
TTFT returns to within 10% of baseline for all reported customers under the original workload within 24 hours of mitigation rollout.
Automated regression test added that simulates mixed-quant fanout warmstart and asserts no >30% tokens/sec drop for 60s after warmstart.
Kernel selector change merged and validated in staging; rollout plan approved and documented.
Customer comms drafted and sent for affected accounts with timeline and mitigation details.
mitigation_plan: Short-term (immediate, <4h): push feature-flag to disable concurrent cross-variant probing in VPC and Dedicated for customers on runtime-1.22. This is a safe gate that prevents simultaneous kernel priming across variants.
Short-term (#2): enable KV cache pinning for warmstarted sessions (pin top-N prefixes) to reduce eviction churn during ramp.
Medium-term (24-72h): introduce token-rate-aware admission control on fanout edges to limit burst concurrency per model variant during warmstart windows.

Long-term (Q2): update kernel-selector heuristics to prefer conservative kernels for initial requests until steady-state token emission is observed; add model-variant compatibility scoring for multi-variant fanout routing.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary feature-flag to 5% of VPC customers with low-risk workloads; monitor TTFT, tokens/sec, and KV eviction rate for 2 hours.
2) If stable, expand to all VPC customers and Dedicated pools in staggered batches over 4 hours.
3) Create emergency rollback toggle for immediate revert if regression observed in unrelated metrics (throughput/TPS).
4) Coordinate with Private deployments: provide patch notes + recommended toggle script and offer remote assistance for critical customers.

postmortem_notes: Root cause appears to be interaction between parallel probing of heterogeneous quant variants and a non-robust kernel-selector that aggressively swaps kernels during initial priming, leading to KV cache oscillation and eviction cascades. Follow-ups: telemetry for kernel decision latency, permanent admission control, and model-compatibility scoring in router. Will complete full postmortem after rollout and telemetry collection.
